title: The Blindspots Between Us: How to Overcome Unconscious Cognitive Bias and Build Better Relationships
author: G.B. (Ginger) Hodges
target_audience: Readers curious about cognitive bias and its effects
Couples, families, and professionals aiming for better communication
core_themes: Unconscious cognitive bias in daily life
How bias impacts relationships and communication
Fostering empathy and understanding across differences
Practical steps for overcoming biased thinking
primary_purpose: To help readers recognize and overcome their own unconscious cognitive biases, enabling them to communicate more effectively, resolve conflicts, and build healthier, more authentic relationships.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, empathetic, and accessible with a blend of psychological insights and practical guidance
structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters progressing from understanding bias to actionable relationship strategies

key_concepts_lessons: Everyone has unconscious biases that shape perceptions and behaviors.
Cognitive bias often creates misunderstandings and distance in relationships.
Awareness and acknowledgment are crucial first steps to overcoming bias.
Empathy and active listening help bridge divides caused by bias.
Intentional strategies—such as reframing thoughts and questioning assumptions—lead to better communication and connection.
Relationships improve when both parties work to recognize and reduce the influence of bias.
notable_features: Focus on bias within close relationships rather than only societal or institutional bias
Includes actionable exercises and self-assessment tools
Merges psychological research with relatable life scenarios
Accessible language for readers without a psychology background
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2020, during a time of heightened awareness and conversation around unconscious bias, diversity, and meaningful communication, particularly in North American and global contexts emphasizing inclusivity and self-improvement.
reception_impact: Praised for its accessible, relatable approach to a complex topic
Valued by readers and practitioners in counseling and coaching fields
Recognized as especially timely given social and cultural divisions
Some critics note its focus on interpersonal rather than systemic aspects of bias
comparable_titles: Blindspot: Hidden Biases of Good People by Mahzarin R. Banaji and Anthony G. Greenwald
Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Crucial Conversations by Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, Ron McMillan, and Al Switzler
Difficult Conversations: How to Discuss What Matters Most by Douglas Stone, Bruce Patton, and Sheila Heen
